transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-05-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~58m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luca (Redwood SE), Rita (Hearthline VP Product), Samir (Head of ML), Evan (SRE)

Summary: Quick QBR-style pulse on usage, costs, reliability signal since pilot start; evaluate go/no-go pilot gate for expanded on-prem demo. Discussed latency hotspots, token economics, SOC2/network questions, and next steps for pricing + technical benchmarks.

Topics: usage trends, cost per token, tail latency, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, VPC/on-prem considerations, SOC2 + KMS, pilot gate metrics, SLOs and rollback plan.

Action items (captured verbally): see metadata list.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to do a short pulse -- sort of a QBR lite for the pilot, go over economics and reliability signals and see if we're good to move to the next gate.
[00:18] Rita: yeah thanks, this timing works. we've been running the recommender and triage assist in prod-ish traffic for two weeks now, approx 150k requests per day. noticed some spikes during morning sync.
[00:35] Samir: traffic's been bursty, 95th p90 latency floated around 420 to 520 ms, p99s hit sometimes 1.6 seconds when model load cold starts.
[00:48] Luca: yeah we saw that, a lot of that is the KV cache warming and cold-starts on the dedicated pods; we suggested a small prefix cache warming during morning ramp which helps bring p99 down ~300-400ms in our local sim.
[01:05] Evan: on our side the SRE flag is the tail latency but also the network egress cost, right now the hosted calls are going to public endpoints and that has some cost and compliance noise.
[01:20] Maya: exactly that's one of the gating items — we usually show three paths: hosted API with VPC peering, Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity in our cloud region, or private (on-prem/VPC) for locked down data. each has different unit economics.
[01:38] Rita: can you give us numbers? we need to compare to our current internal GPU infra run-rate.
[01:44] Maya: sure, at current cambridge config (quantized 4-bit), rough numbers: hosted default path gives best time-to-market but unit cost ~ $0.012 /k token at your volume; dedicated reserved drops to ~ $0.007 /k tokens but you take on a monthly commit; private on-prem depends on your hardware but we'd estimate parity to dedicated plus ops overhead. these are rough — we'll send a spreadsheet.
[02:10] Samir: small nit though, how do you account for batching? our request distribution is many short sequences which kills batching efficiency.
[02:22] Luca: good question. we profiled your trace -- average seq len 48 tokens, but a long tail. Redwood runtime uses continuous batching and prefix KV cache to reduce per-token compute; for your profile we recommended conservative batching (max batch 32) and a 24hr prefix cache window to avoid cold starts for frequent items. that improved throughput in our sim.
[02:50] Evan: you said KV cache -- I heard KV cash earlier in your doc, just flagging the term might get misread in our legal deck.
[02:57] Maya: noted.
[03:05] Rita: on security front, legal asked for SOC2 Type II evidence, network flow logs, and KMS proof for key isolation. are those in your docs?
[03:16] Maya: yes SOC2 report and SOC cover are in our security pack. we also have network diagram (we can redact) and KMS integrations (AWS KMS and customer-managed HSM) details. Luca can pull the SOC2 summary.
[03:29] Luca: I will share the security kit after this call and include the HSM notes and audit log retention options.
[03:36] Samir: what about data retention — for inference logs we don't want PII retained more than 30 days ideally. can you do short retention?
[03:45] Maya: yes configurable; hosted default is 90 days for metrics but we offer 30-day retention for inference payloads on pilot, and private deployments you control retention.
[03:53] Evan: network controls question — do you support egress-only endpoints or strictly peered VPC?
[04:00] Luca: we support VPC peering and private endpoints; egress-only isn't typical but can be arranged with our infra team for on-prem setups. there have been instances where customers request explicit firewall rules and we provide IP ranges and certs.
[04:16] Rita: returning to economics: you mentioned burst capacity as an add-on — can you quantify the cost of a weekend spike to 4x baseline?
[04:26] Maya: short answer: burst is charged as a short-term rate above reserved commit; example: if your reserved commit covers 2k rps and you hit 8k for 3 hours, the burst fee would be proportional to delta usage; we'll line-item that in the pilot pricing sheet.
[04:43] Samir: one operational question — model rollouts. if we roll a model that regresses, what's the fallback?
[04:50] Luca: our platform supports route-based rollouts and automatic rollback to a pinned variant if quality/regression monitors trigger. seeding traffic split and canary thresholds are configurable. we also integrate eval hooks so you can run post-deploy prompt set checks.
[05:06] Rita: good. the pilot gate we care about: uptime >= 99.9% during business hours, p95 < 500ms, p99 < 1s for 80% of traffic, and no security redlines. are those feasible?
[05:18] Luca: feasible with dedicated capacity and prefix cache tuning. Hosted path can meet it too but you'd want dedicated for stricter latency SLOs. We'll propose the config that meets those gates.
[05:30] Evan: timeline question: we want to move to the on-prem demo for the larger platform team inside three weeks. what do you need from us?
[05:37] Maya: a go/no-go checklist: signed pilot amendment, list of infra contacts (Evan), compliance contact, and sample traffic for benchmark. Also sign-off on SLA gates. Once we have that, Redwood SE runs a pre-demo stress test and we schedule the on-prem demo.
[05:53] Rita: legal will need the security kit and a small contract redline window (5 business days).
[06:00] Maya: fine. We'll target sending pricing and security kit by EOW.
[06:05] [Speaker 1]: (mumbled) also please include the rollback playbook.
[06:10] Luca: yes, we'll attach the rollback playbook and a runbook for incident response.
[06:14] Samir: quick technical ask — can Redwood expose per-route token cost so we can attribute spend to features?
[06:22] Maya: yes, console exposes token-level breakdown by route, model, and token-class. that's in the console beta. we'll include screenshots.
[06:30] Evan: any concerns about model quantization affecting quality for our triage model? we've been sensitive to hallucinations.
[06:38] Luca: quantization can slightly change logits; we do quality evals using your prompt set and report delta. if it's outside your tolerance, we recommend a higher precision profile for that model class.
[06:50] Rita: last thing, who is our direct Redwood contact during the pilot?
[06:55] Maya: I'll be your AE; Luca is the SE who will run tests and the demo. You can loop in Maya@redwood.com and Luca@redwood.com.
[07:02] Samir: ok sounds good. next steps recap?
[07:06] Maya: recap: Maya send pricing + pilot spreadsheet; Luca send latency heatmap and KV cache config; Redwood send SOC2 + network diagram; schedule on-prem deep dive w/ Evan; customer to confirm gate metrics and legal timeframe.
[07:25] Rita: thanks all, this was helpful. we'll review and aim to come back with the gate decision by 2027-05-11.
[07:32] Maya: great thanks everyone. end.

Notes: occasional transcription errors present (e.g. KV cache vs KV cash, VPCP). Attachments referenced: pilot_pricing_v2.xlsx, redwood_security_kit_v1.pdf, latency_heatmap.png.
